rendered_prompt:
These CORE requirements have no task covering them yet (a task covers a requirement by listing its id in requirement_ids):
- R-016: Stats show daily review-count history.
- R-017: Stats show retention rate (% graded Good/Easy).
- R-018: All stats screens handle empty and sparse data gracefully with honest, designed empty states — never a crash or misleading placeholder.
- R-019: Demo-seeded decks/cards are excluded by default from aggregate/overall stats and streak calculations.
- R-020: CSV export produces front, back, and optional note columns.
- R-021: CSV import accepts front (required), back (required), and note (optional) columns, with a preview step before any data is committed.
- R-022: CSV import preview enumerates a distinct, visible error reason for every malformed-row case: empty front/back, wrong column count, embedded commas/quotes, bad encoding/BOM, CRLF vs LF — never silently dropped.
- R-023: CSV import flags duplicates as case-sensitive exact front+back matches, both within the imported file and against existing non-archived cards in the target deck, as their own distinct reason.
- R-024: Export then re-import round-trips losslessly, including notes.
- R-025: CSV import test fixtures include at least one real-world exported CSV in addition to hand-crafted edge cases.
- R-026: One optional local daily reminder notification fires at a user-chosen time.
- R-027: The notification body contains only a numeric due-card count — never card content, deck names, or subject matter.
- R-028: No notification is scheduled or fires when the computed due count is 0.
- R-029: The due count is recomputed at natural refresh points (foreground, background, post-session, day rollover) rather than fixed at scheduling time.
- R-030: Notification permission denial is handled gracefully with no crash and a clear path to opt in later.

Re-emit a SINGLE corrected ```tasks-json``` fenced block — the whole backlog, not a diff — that adds or updates tasks (via requirement_ids) so every one of these is covered by at least one task.
MACHINE CONTRACT (required): in your wrap-up, alongside the prose, emit ONE fenced ```tasks-json``` block containing a single JSON object of the form {"tasks": [{"id": "T-001", "title": ..., "owner_lane": ..., "files": [...], "depends_on": [], "acceptance_criteria": [...], "requirement_ids": ["R-001"], "status": "pending"}]}. owner_lane must be one of: data_domain, primary_ui, services_utilities, polish_resilience. depends_on lists task ids and the graph must be acyclic. requirement_ids lists the id(s) from requirements.json this task fulfills — every CORE requirement needs at least one task naming it, or the build is missing part of what was promised. The build workers are assigned their lane's tasks from this block, so make it complete.
